name: Baby Rubber Plant
description: Peperomia obtusifolia, commonly known as the baby rubber plant or pepper face, is a compact evergreen perennial in the Piperaceae family, native to tropical regions from Mexico and southern Florida through Central and South America. It grows as a bushy upright plant with thick, waxy, elliptic dark green leaves on erect stems, typically reaching about 30 cm indoors. The semi-succulent foliage stores water, making it more drought-tolerant than many tropical houseplants. It prefers bright indirect light but tolerates lower light for solid green forms; variegated cultivars need brighter conditions to maintain color. Allow the top few centimeters of soil to dry between waterings and avoid soggy conditions to prevent root rot. It tolerates average household humidity (40–60%) and thrives in warm rooms around 18–24 °C. Small greenish-white flower spikes appear occasionally but are not showy. Non-toxic to cats, dogs, and humans. Many variegated cultivars exist, including 'Variegata' and 'Alba'.
careTips: Provide bright indirect light; solid green forms tolerate lower light, variegated forms need more
Allow the top 2–3 cm of soil to dry before watering; semi-succulent leaves store moisture
Use well-draining potting mix with perlite or bark; avoid waterlogged soil
Tolerates average room humidity (40–60%); higher humidity is beneficial in summer
Keep temperatures between 18–24 °C; protect from cold drafts and temperatures below 10 °C
Fertilize monthly at half strength during spring and summer only
Propagate easily from stem or leaf cuttings
Non-toxic and safe for homes with pets
geographicOrigin: Tropical Americas (Mexico to South America, southern Florida)
